lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Independent application: recognising when to seek help urgently

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic recognising when to seek help urgently task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner is given five fictional situations, each describing a different physical concern with different severity and timing.
safetyNotes: All five situations are fictional and provided in this lesson; no real personal concern of the learner's own is required or requested anywhere in this task.
If a learner has a real concern while completing this lesson, they should raise it separately with a trusted adult rather than substituting it into this assignment.
materials: learner-local: the five provided fictional situations

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l05-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l05-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l05-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l05-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: What is one general rule (not tied to any single situation above) that you'll use to decide how urgently to act, going forward?

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g11-u03-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Classification accuracy and reasoning: Most classifications correctly match the urgency level suggested by the specific signs in each situation. | Use of specific signs vs. general impression: Reasoning cites a specific, named detail from the situation. | Generalized rule quality: Rule is general and could reasonably be applied to a new, unseen situation. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner write one additional fictional situation of their own for a category not already well-represented above, classify it, and explain the specific signs that justify that classification.

resources.title: recognising when to seek help urgently worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner is given five fictional situations, each describing a different physical concern with different severity and timing.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact recognising when to seek help urgently decision or action.
Model move 2: Before working through the situations below, write down what you currently use to decide whether something needs attention right away versus can wait.

resources.title: recognising when to seek help urgently action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for recognising when to seek help urgently.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.

resources.title: recognising when to seek help urgently coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner is given five fictional situations, each describing a different physical concern with different severity and timing.
Coach direction: Before working through the situations below, write down what you currently use to decide whether something needs attention right away versus can wait.
Learner prompt: What rule or gut feeling do you currently use to decide whether something needs attention right away versus can wait -- even if you're not fully confident in it?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: recognising when to seek help urgently complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: For each fictional situation below, choose the urgency category that fits best.
Response 1 (t2-p1): Situation A: A person suddenly can't lift one arm all the way and the corner of their mouth is drooping on one side; it started a few minutes ago.
Response 2 (t2-p2): Situation B: A person has had a mild, dull headache for a few hours after a long day of screen time, with no other symptoms.
Response 3 (t2-p3): Situation C: A person cut their hand on a kitchen knife and the bleeding hasn't slowed after ten minutes of firm, direct pressure.
Response 4 (t2-p4): Situation D: A person has had a cough for two weeks that isn't getting better and is starting to interrupt their sleep, with no fever.
Response 5 (t2-p5): Situation E: A person twisted their ankle yesterday; it's swollen and uncomfortable to walk on, but they can move their toes and there's no visible deformity.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: recognising when to seek help urgently minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: What is one general rule (not tied to any single situation above) that you'll use to decide how urgently to act, going forward?

Success checks: Classification accuracy and reasoning: Most classifications correctly match the urgency level suggested by the specific signs in each situation. | Use of specific signs vs. general impression: Reasoning cites a specific, named detail from the situation. | Generalized rule quality: Rule is general and could reasonably be applied to a new, unseen situation.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: recognising when to seek help urgently supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g11-u03-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional recognising when to seek help urgently condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Classification accuracy and reasoning: Most classifications correctly match the urgency level suggested by the specific signs in each situation. | Use of specific signs vs. general impression: Reasoning cites a specific, named detail from the situation. | Generalized rule quality: Rule is general and could reasonably be applied to a new, unseen situation..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g11-u03-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
